body:
1. @Configuration & @Bean: The Custom Workshop

Think of this as your 'Custom Workshop.' While Spring usually builds things automatically, sometimes you want to build a tool yourself (like a 3rd party library) and tell Spring, 'Hey, keep this in the warehouse for me!'

2. @Controller & @RequestMapping: The Receptionist

The @Controller is the Receptionist. @RequestMapping is the Directory. It tells the user, 'If you want to talk to Sales, go to Desk A; if you want Support, go to Desk B.'

3. @Qualifier: The Name Tag

Imagine two workers (Beans) who both know how to fix a car, but one is a Junior and one is a Senior. If you just ask for a 'Worker,' Spring gets confused. @Qualifier is like checking their Name Tag to pick the right one.

4. @PathVariable vs @RequestParam: The Address vs The Package

@PathVariable is part of the Address (like the house number). @RequestParam is like a Note attached to the package (extra info like 'fragile' or 'color=blue').

5. @RequestBody: The JSON Mailbox

When someone sends you a complex package (a JSON object), @RequestBody tells Spring to open the box, read the contents, and automatically turn it into a Java Object you can work with.

6. @Primary: The Default Choice

If you have multiple workers but don't want to use a name tag every time, use @Primary. It’s like saying, 'If I don't specify, this is my favorite/default worker to use.'

7. @ConditionalOnProperty: The Smart Switch

This is a 'Power Switch.' The Bean is only created if a specific setting is turned 'ON' in your config file. Great for features that are still in 'Beta' or testing.
